hook.line: There are five main types of content you should be posting.
hook.visual: Creator outdoors holding a mic and laptop under a lime '5 MAIN TYPES of Content' title, with a five-slice wheel of thumbnails labelled with each type.

beats.what: Title and a five-slice content wheel diagram appear with the list promise.
Cut to her second character (blue hoodie, water bottle) reacting: five is too many.
Number 1 'EDUCATIONAL' in lime with a row of example thumbnails.
Number 2 'STORYTELLING' title; the doubter asks for ideas.
Full lime card with three example formats and their hook lines.
Doubter says series are 'POPULAR' lately, in big lime text.
Lime 'SERIES TYPE' card with three series formats.
Number 5 'double down': an OG video next to a grid of its remakes.
Doubter asks where to learn this; the answer 'I FOLLOW AVA' with an Instagram follow chip.

characters.who: The creator playing a skeptical friend (blue hoodie, water bottle)
characters.enters: Hard cut at 2.4 s right after the list promise, reacting with disbelief.
characters.acts: Asks the questions a viewer would (what are they, any ideas, how), so each answer has a setup.
characters.exits: Hard cut back to the expert after each question.

why_it_works: A doubter character voices the viewer's objection, so every list item arrives as an answer to a question.
Cuts every 1.8 s median alternate the two characters, which keeps the 52 s list moving.
Each item gets a big lime title plus example thumbnails, so the list is skimmable and saveable (826 shares).
The follow CTA is the skit's punchline ('I follow Ava'), so it doesn't feel like an ask.
weaknesses: Example thumbnails and the format cards are too small to read without pausing.
Number four and five are rushed compared with the first three.
for_robert: Give Fred the doubter role: he cuts in with the viewer's question ('five of what?') and Robert answers, and the follow CTA lands as Fred's punchline.
